cases.summary: Every positive Morita dual has the same based ring. In the specified order-32 near-group construction route, the parent group must be C4 × C2³. Compatible pointed data exist, but the parent category and required algebra are unconstructed. General categorification remains unresolved.

same_category_implications.explanation: The uniform argument for the generalized near-group family R′(m), applied at m=4, proves that every categorification admits a spherical structure. No pivotality assumption is needed.

existence_implications.explanation: Every categorification has a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate with the same fusion ring. Thus general and pseudo-unitary categorifiability are equivalent as existence questions. This does not assert pseudo-unitarity of every original categorification or imply unitarity.

invariants.exact_dimension_method: Each FP dimension is the largest real root of its displayed irreducible polynomial, isolated by the rational interval. invariants.fusion_matrix_convention: N_i[j][k] = N[i][j][k]; rows are the right input basis index, columns are the output basis index.

braided.explanation: The fusion ring is noncommutative: N[1,3,5]=1, whereas N[3,1,5]=2. A braiding would identify the two tensor products and force equal multiplicities. No pivotality assumption is needed.

morita.explanation: Every proper fusion subcategory is pointed and the global FP dimension is irrational. A braided Morita representative would therefore give a braiding on this category, by the tensor-image criterion. Hence no categorification of this ring is Morita equivalent to a braided fusion category.
